hero.subtitle: Celebrating emerging filmmakers and their creative visions

about.title: About the Festival
about.mission_text: The Nido Film Festival is dedicated to showcasing innovative short films from emerging filmmakers worldwide. We provide a platform for creative voices to be heard and celebrated, fostering a community of artists who push the boundaries of storytelling through film.
about.info_paragraph: 2026 marks the first year of NestFest! NestFest takes participants from all levels of education all over Latin America, hoping to create an intergenerational celebration of talent and art. Selected short films (3-10 minutes) will be screened live at Nido on April 30th, while also being streamed online. Selectees will be reached out with invitations to Nido for the event. The festival features an award ceremony, food and speeches from the judges. Submitting to NestFest is absolutely free and a great opportunity for upcoming filmmakers to get publicity and recognition for their achievements.
about.about_nido: Nido de Águilas is a private school in Santiago Chile. Founded by Waldo Stevenson in 1934, Nido empowers learners to connect authentically, explore with curiosity, and act with purpose. It offers a profound film education, with courses in digital filmmaking, stagecraft, and IB Film.

david_gran.name: David Gran
david_gran.description: David Gran has been teaching Film for over 20 years. He has worked on the development of the official IB Curriculum, he's been a film examiner, and is the author of InThinking's DP Film page. He began teaching film to middle school students in Harlem, and has taught high school level film classes in New York, Shanghai and now in Santiago at the International School Nido de Aguilas. Next year he will be moving to Thailand to teach at the International School of Bangkok. His favorite film is Three Idiots and insists it's a better film than you might think from hearing the title.

jonas_hekel.name: Jonas Hekel
jonas_hekel.description: Jonas Hekel is a working filmmaker and Nido de Aguilas alumni. His work includes advertising for the US Government, freelance creative filmmaking, and directing production at his church.

toc.title: Terms & Conditions
toc.intro: By submitting a film to NestFest, you agree to the following terms and conditions:
toc.contact: For any questions, please contact: jonashekel@students.nido.cl

eligibility.title: 1. Eligibility
eligibility.content: Submissions must be created by students currently enrolled in a secondary or post-secondary institution, or who have graduated within the past 12 months. The festival reserves the right to request proof of student status.

originality.title: 2. Originality & Rights
originality.content1: Entrants must hold full rights to all content within their film, including music, images, and performances. By submitting, you confirm that your work does not infringe on any copyright, trademark, or intellectual property rights.
originality.content2: In cases where a college, university, or other institution retains full or partial ownership of the submitted film or any of its components (including as part of coursework, equipment use agreements, or institutional policies), the entrant must have obtained all required permissions from that institution to submit the work to the festival. By submitting, you confirm that such permissions have been secured and that the screening and promotional use of the film by the festival does not violate any institutional agreements or intellectual property policies.
originality.content3: Entrants further warrant that their submission does not infringe on any copyright, trademark, or other intellectual property rights.

contentGuidelines.title: 3. Content Guidelines
contentGuidelines.content: Films must not contain unlawful, defamatory, or excessively explicit material. The festival reserves the right to disqualify any submission deemed inappropriate or not aligned with the festival's values.

submissionFormat.title: 4. Submission Format
submissionFormat.content: All films must be submitted in the specified digital format and within the stated runtime limits. Late or incomplete submissions may not be considered.

usageRights.title: 5. Usage Rights
usageRights.content: By submitting, you grant the festival a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to screen your film during the festival and to use excerpts, stills, and your film's title for promotional purposes.

judging.title: 6. Judging & Selection
judging.content: All submissions will be reviewed by a panel of judges. Decisions regarding selection and awards are final and not subject to appeal.

liability.title: 7. Liability
liability.content: The festival is not responsible for any technical issues, data loss, or damages related to submission materials.

agreement.title: 8. Agreement
agreement.content: Submission of a film constitutes full acceptance of these terms and conditions.
